newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No big inflation pressure from high dlr - Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: No big inflation pressure from high dlr - Gaddum.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum told weekly newspaper The European Voice on Friday the dollar was currently overvalued, but could not see any large inflationary pressures at present.
"There is a slight overvaluation of the dollar showing itself," Gaddum said. He gave the interview on July 17, a Bundesbank official said later today.
"This might lead to price pressure on imports. Large inflationary pressures cannot be seen for the moment," he added.

Gaddum said he favoured an early decision on the rates at which European currencies participating in economic and monetary union (EMU) will be set against the future European single currency, the euro.
"An early announcement of the procedures for setting the conversion rates might reduce currency speculation."

Gaddum said he expected discussions on EMU parities to intensify "during the autumn". But he thought the current central parities in Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) formed a good basis for the future EMU rates.

"I think that central ERM rates are a good basis for setting the conversion rates at which the currencies of the participating countries are irrevocably fixed," he told the Brussels-based European Voice.
The euro is to start on January 1, 1999 with the EU countries which meet strict budget and debt criteria.
